Anya V: quick idea: "maintenance_mode" runtime flag per-tenant. goal: let ops safely shed traffic during infra windows without manual network changes.

Sasha K: I like it. what levels are you thinking? soft drain vs hard block?

Anya V: thinking levels: off, shadow (observe only), gradual (percent shed), block (deny). controller should honor telemetry gates and auto-pause/rollback.

Miguel R: API shape question: do we embed the ramp in the flag or reference a separate policy? some tenants need complex splits (e.g., 90/10 across regions).

Anya V: prefer minimal flag and optional policy_ref. sample apply: 
```
POST /api/v1/flags/apply
{
  \"target\": \"tenant:acme\",
  \"flag\": \"maintenance_mode\",
  \"mode\": \"gradual\",
  \"policy_ref\": \"policies/maint/v1\",
  \"actor\": \"anya@redwood\",
  \"reason\": \"db migration window\"
}
```

Sasha K: telemetry gating needs clear signals/thresholds. propose per-tenant baseline comparisons for latency and error-rate; e.g., p50 +30% or p95 +20% or err_rate_above 0.5%.

Jen (oncall): strongly prefer per-tenant baselines. global thresholds might abort a rollout because of one noisy big tenant. add a min-volume threshold so tiny tenants don't gate.

Miguel R: console should show gate status (pass/warn/fail), last eval time, and quick rollback button. also link to traces and allow exporting the gate evaluation payload for audits.

Console UI: can do a compact card with 15m sparkline and the gate rule that fired. but we'll need a metrics endpoint that returns pre-computed gate stats (not raw samples).

Anya V: telemetry contract draft: GET /api/v1/flags/{flag}/gates?tenant=ID -> returns 1m-bucketed array for last 30m of {baseline_p50,current_p50,p50_pct_change,p95_pct_change,err_rate,volume}. rollout-controller decides gate outcome server-side.

Sasha K: also compute both absolute and relative conditions in policy: absolute_err_rate_threshold + relative_pct_change. Example: absolute 0.5% OR relative > 40% => gate fail.

Jen (oncall): add guard: if volume < 100 reqs/min => treat as shadow/dry-run. Also log audit event for every mode change with actor, commit sha, and policy id.

Miguel R: controller implementation notes: lease per-tenant, persistent state in config-store with an oplog for audits, idempotent apply, and metric emission under rollout.controller.* (progress,gates,fails,transitions). tracing spans: rollout.apply -> policy.eval -> shaper.apply.

Anya V: ops checklist for a rollout: 1) create policy (thresholds + ramp), 2) dry-shadow 10-15m, 3) gradual ramp (configurable steps e.g. [10,25,50,100] with pause windows), 4) gated decision-making and auto-rollback on failures, 5) full-block only manual or after sustained pass.

Sasha K: allow policy to specify cohort order (weighted cohorts) so we can target blue group first. also make ramp configurable per-policy.

Miguel R: add API idempotency token to prevent concurrent apply conflicts. controller should return a well-defined state machine (queued, ramping, paused, failed, rolled_back, done).

Jen (oncall): emergency rollback snippet for runbook: 
1) curl -X POST /api/v1/flags/apply -d '{\"target\":\"tenant:ALL\",\"flag\":\"maintenance_mode\",\"mode\":\"off\",\"actor\":\"oncall\",\"reason\":\"emergency rollback\"}'
2) verify audit entry and controller state == off
3) notify customers via status page

Anya V: deprecation: flags should optionally include expires_at and remind_before fields so owners get notified before expiry. also include owner contact in policy metadata.

Console UI: will add owner reminders + an explain modal that shows which rule tripped (absolute vs relative) and the raw numeric values used in eval.

Sasha K: next steps?

Anya V: i'll write an RFC: api surfaces, policy schema, telemetry contract, controller design, console mocks, runbook. requesting reviews from @Miguel R and @Jen (oncall).

Miguel R: i'll review, will add notes on backpressure and collision handling.

Jen (oncall): +1. i'll validate the runbook in staging after the RFC lands.
